I'm good.

Eight years ago, went out on my own as sort of a CMO for hire.

I wanted to get out of the hourly rate business and get into a recurring revenue business model.
So I started reselling CRM software like SharpSpring, which is a Marketo HubSpot competitor that was ultimately acquired by Constant Contact.
And I was looking for what other marketing software can I resell.
I want to make money in my sleep.
And I came upon a reputation management software and said, okay, I could sell that.
So I started selling that to my clients and I'm like, this is going somewhere.
But what quickly happened, Andy, was clients started to cancel.
They started to cancel their subscriptions.
I said, what?
Why are you canceling this?
Because we don't use it.
It's too hard, it's too messy.
We have to do all this with lists and we have to do campaigns and we can't REM our password.
I said, shit, I got to do something, right?
So pivot number one was, was shifting from marketing services to reseller.

I'm selling you the limousine and then, and then you're paying me to drive you around in it.
And so that started taking off.
This was in 2018.
And eventually my reputation management business started to eclipse my marketing services business, which was great because I wanted recurring revenue.
My third pivot was to white label the reputation management software that I was reselling.
So now it was labeled as repster from Tool and Associates, even though it was third party software that I was paying royalties for and see where, where it went from there.
Once I white labeled the actual software that was doing all of the work that I was actually getting paid to do, I could switch out the software underneath the covers and no one would know.
So two and a half years ago I built my own reputation management software platform, replaced what I was paying third party vendors to license from them, and now I own all the intellectual property.
Fast forward.
We now have over 400 individual client locations throughout North America using our online review Service.
They're on 12 month agreements billed monthly through ACH.
And we built up quite a nice business.
We grew 80% last year, 2024 over 23, which was a nice growth.
We've already brought in another 25% growth year to date since the end of 2024.
So we're on a nice growth trajectory.
I own the business.
I have no debt, no outside investment, no partners, no loans, nothing.
Right?
Don't even have a credit card.
So it's a very, it's a very nice business model.
Just to go bring back to the beginning when I said we do a lot more than reputation management.

We go one step Further, we get negative reviews deleted for our clients from Google, Yelp and Facebook.
Any other review software product isn't going to do that at all because they're software.
So we're kind of an aggregate.
Andy.
We're a software company, but with services capabilities that add on top of software platform.

Highly leveraged.

I'm doing very well.
The business is doing very well.

Right.

Okay.
Brilliant.
Yeah.

And I wasn't quite sure whether that was indicative of the business or, or not.
Like you say, yeah, maybe it pays to have no reputation when you manage other people's reputations.
But look, it sounds like a solid business and certainly 1 million EBITDA each year is obviously extremely valuable.
And I'm sure you know that software businesses are valued very differently from how marketing agencies are valued.
I'm sure that's why you put the effort in the first place.
Also a genius move, by the way, white labeling somebody else's services first before building your own.
I mean that's the way to do it, isn't it?
Build the demand first and then.
No, it's great.

Yeah.
Amazing.

And so, and, and it gave me the time to build up my revenue stream to fund the development initiative.
I've never had to borrow money for, for, for development.

Okay.

Would you like to earn a $25 credit at this business?

We're saying, great, you just told the whole world how happy you are.

Yeah.
Yes.
Genius.
Okay.

Andy Day introduced his firm, Capital A, which specializes in M&A advisory services for marketing agencies, proposing the idea of listing Toole's business on the Agencies Co marketplace to attract potential buyers. The conversation included insights on the unique business model of Toole's company, its high profitability, and a possible valuation strategy focusing on adjusted EBITDA, suggesting it may be valued like a software firm. Action items included Andy sending listing information to Steven and Steven considering the listing to explore sale opportunities.
